========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Special messages? I don’t know… not like a TV talking to me or anything like that, if that’s what you mean.

It’s more that the chart doesn’t match what I saw. That’s why I’m here. For the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. And everyone keeps saying the numbers are fine—doctors, my family, everybody—but that doesn’t explain why it was one way and then later it wasn’t.

I mean, when you work around labs, you notice details. I’m a phlebotomist, so I know people miss things, or they act like you don’t understand because you’re “too close” to it. My aunt does that too, she’ll say, “Just listen to the doctor,” like that ends the conversation. But it doesn’t.

So… hidden signs meant for me, no, I don’t think of it like that. It’s the records. The mismatch. That’s what I keep coming back to, and it’s been wearing me down.

And it’s not even just about one number—well, it started that way, but then you start noticing how everyone acts like you’re bothering them just for asking. My family says I’m stressing myself out, and maybe I am, but I wouldn’t be if someone would just admit the records aren’t right or show me where the missing parts went.\n\nDoctor: Is it possible that you might be mistaken about someone in the clinic changing or withholding your dad’s lab results?\n\nPatient: I mean… I guess anyone can be mistaken about little things, like maybe I wrote down a time wrong or misread a label when I was tired, but not this. Not the whole thing.\n\nFor the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and people keep telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family, everybody—but the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It just doesn’t. And I know people think I’m stuck on it, but if you worked around labs like I do, you’d understand why it bothers me. It’s been wearing me down because I keep trying to explain it and everyone acts like I’m making trouble instead of just looking at what’s missing.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to hear or see?\n\nPatient: I don’t… I don’t think so. Not like seeing a person in the room or hearing voices, if that’s what you mean. I mean, sometimes I notice things other people don’t notice, but that’s different—like when a form is worded weirdly or a number doesn’t match the way it should.\n\nAt work you kind of train yourself to catch little details, you know? People act like noticing details is the problem, but if nobody noticed details in a lab, everything would fall apart. So… no, I don’t think I’m hearing or seeing things. I’m just paying attention.\n\nDoctor: Do you think other people are trying to harm, deceive, or plot against you in areas of your life besides your dad’s lab results?\n\nPatient: Not really… I mean, not in the same way. I don’t walk around thinking everyone is out to get me or something.\n\nIt’s this clinic situation with my dad’s labs. That’s the thing I can’t let go of, because for almost a year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in that system is changing something or holding parts back, and every time they tell me the numbers are fine it just makes me feel like they’re not looking at the same chart I saw. And then my family says I’m wearing myself down, which… I am, I know I am, but if someone would just show me the missing pieces instead of brushing me off, I wouldn’t have to keep chasing it.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel driven to repeatedly check the records or ask for reassurance about your dad’s lab results, even when you try not to?\n\nPatient: Yes… I mean, I try not to call it “reassurance,” because that makes it sound like I just want someone to pat me on the head and say it’s okay. I want the actual chart to make sense.\n\nBut yeah, I check. I go back over what I have, the dates, the numbers, what was released and what wasn’t. Sometimes I’ll tell myself I’m not going to look at it that night, and then I end up opening it again because it’s like… if I can just find the one place where it doesn’t line up, then maybe they’ll stop saying I’m imagining it.\n\nAnd it’s not like I enjoy doing that. I’m tired. I’ve been doing this for almost a year, trying to prove someone in that clinic system is changing something or holding parts of my dad’s results back, and everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine. My family, doctors—everybody. But the chart doesn’t match what I saw. It just doesn’t. So yes, I keep checking, because if I don’t, then it feels like I’m letting them get away with it.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel that your urge to keep checking your dad’s lab records is unreasonable or excessive?\n\nPatient: Unreasonable… I don’t know. Excessive, maybe, if you look at how much time it takes. I mean, I’m here because this has been going on for almost a year, and I know it’s wearing me down.\n\nBut I can’t just say it’s unreasonable, because the chart doesn’t match what I saw. That’s the part everyone skips over. My family keeps saying, “You need to let this go,” and the doctors say the numbers are fine, but they weren’t the same—something in the clinic system is changing it or holding parts back, and if I stop checking, then what? Then it just gets buried.\n\nAnd I know I go in circles with it. So yes, it’s… it’s too much in the sense that I’m exhausted. I don’t want to be thinking about it all the time, obviously. I’ll be trying to make dinner or driving somewhere and suddenly I’m back on that chart in my head, like the numbers, the dates, what was shown and what wasn’t.\n\nIt’s been almost a year of this. I’m here because I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing something or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and everyone—doctors, my family—keeps telling me the numbers are fine. But the chart doesn’t match what I saw.\n\nSo yes, it comes into my mind even when I’m trying to focus on something else. But it’s not random, you know? It’s because something is wrong there, and I can’t just pretend I didn’t see it.\n\nDoctor: Has there ever been a moment when you fully believed you might be wrong about the clinic changing or withholding your dad’s lab results?\n\nPatient: Fully believed I might be wrong? No… not fully. I’ve had moments where I’m tired enough that I think, okay, maybe I missed something, maybe I’m not explaining it right. Like when my family keeps saying the numbers are fine, or the doctors say there’s nothing there, I try to sit with that for a second.\n\nBut then I go back to the chart, and it still doesn’t match what I saw. And I know how lab records are supposed to look—I mean, I’ve worked around this stuff, I’m not just making up numbers out of thin air. Sorry, that’s probably not what you asked exactly. But fully believe I’m wrong? No. Not when the chart doesn’t line up.\n\nDoctor: Outside of this issue with your dad’s lab results, have you had times when your thoughts felt jumbled or people had trouble following what you were saying?\n\nPatient: I don’t… I don’t think so? I mean, people have told me I go on too long sometimes, but that’s usually because they’re not listening to the part that matters.\n\nOutside of my dad’s records, I guess I can get sidetracked. Like at work, if someone asks me something simple, I might explain the whole background because otherwise people misunderstand things, and then suddenly they’re looking at me like I’m making it complicated. But jumbled? I don’t know. That sounds like I’m not making sense, and I don’t think that’s what’s happening.\n\nSometimes I probably talk around the point. I’m doing it now, probably. But I haven’t really noticed people not being able to follow me unless they already don’t want to hear what I’m saying.\n\nDoctor: When this started, were you going through a period of feeling unusually depressed?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. I mean, I was upset, definitely, but it was more because things weren’t lining up and nobody seemed to want to look at it the way I was seeing it.\n\nWhen you say “unusually depressed,” do you mean like sad for no reason, or not functioning? Because I don’t really know how to separate that from being stressed when something serious is happening. I remember being preoccupied with it, and frustrated, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing as depression.\n\nDoctor: Over the past year, have you become much less interested in seeing people or doing your usual activities?\n\nPatient: I don’t know if I’d say “much less interested.” I mean, I still see people when I need to, and I still do things, but it’s harder when every conversation turns into someone telling me to “let it go,” like that’s helpful.\n\nSo maybe I’ve pulled back some, but not because I suddenly don’t care about people or activities. It’s more like… if I go to dinner with my sister and she brings up how I’m “stuck on this,” then the whole night changes, and I’m sitting there thinking about what she doesn’t understand. I guess I haven’t really been keeping track that way.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever filed a formal complaint or contacted authorities because you believed the clinic was altering your dad’s lab results?\n\nPatient: I mean… I’ve thought about it. But I’ve been trying to get someone to take it seriously, because it’s wearing me down.\n\nDoctor: Has this belief about your dad’s lab results ever led you to think you were receiving special messages or hidden signs meant specifically for you?\n\nPatient: Special messages?
